headline: South Asia: 'We're a tech-savvy army': DG ISPR voices confidence in Pakistan's operational readiness for drone warfare
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: 'We're a tech-savvy army': DG ISPR voices confidence in Pakistan's operational readiness for drone warfare.
- India: China's mysterious submarine could give US Navy a Pacific nightmare.
- Western Russia: Girl and woman killed and four injured in Russian attack on Vinnytsia Oblast – photos.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Low-altitude Air Force One Halloween flyover rattles DC residents.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Low-altitude Air Force One Halloween flyover rattles DC residents.
During a White House Halloween celebration, trick-or-treaters and D.C. residents were surprised with a flyover that left some unsettled by its low altitude and only 15-minute warning.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Girl and woman killed and four injured in Russian attack on Vinnytsia Oblast – photos.
Ternopil Oblast head has confirmed two people killed and three children injured as a result of a Russian strike on the Koziatyn hromada.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: "Enough to fill 200 Moscow Metro carriages": Zelenskyy reports record Russian losses in October.
Zelenskyy has said Russia lost 54,400 troops killed and wounded in October, its highest monthly figure since the war began, while Ukraine liberated 96.2 sq km of territory.
- The Moscow Times, Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, just now: Russia's FSB Says Minor Detained Over Moscow Park Attack Threat After U.S. Tip-Off.
The U.S. Embassy in Moscow had issued an urgent security alert warning of a credible threat of a mass casualty event.
- The Moscow Times, 3 hours ago: Russia’s Statistics Agency Hit by Cyberattack as Hackers Claim Massive Data Theft.
Hackers claimed to have stolen 23 terabytes of data, including information on Russian losses in the war in Ukraine.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Russian strikes leave thousands without power in Ukraine, says Zelenskyy.
- Politico Europe, Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian strikes leave thousands without power in Ukraine, says Zelenskyy.
The Ukrainian president's remarks came as Moscow reported "significant damage" to an industrial facility in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region.

AFRICA

- Africanews, one day ago: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses.
Multiple drone strikes have hit northern regions of Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians, including children, witnesses and a medical source said on Friday
- Africanews, one day ago: 2,000 Salvadoran troops take quarters in Haiti to help fight gangs.
The deployment followed a gang attack on four Salvadoran members of the Gang Suppression Force who went missing
- Africanews, 2 days ago: President Ruto seeks compensation for Kenyans recruited into Russian military.
An investigation by Journalists for Justice, published earlier this month, identified at least 76 Kenyans killed while fighting for Russia, alongside 841 Kenyan nationals recruited between October 2022 and June 2026.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 days ago: Nigeria: How to Prevent Another Attack in Taraba Beyond Security Deployment.
[Daily Trust] The latest attack on Binnari community in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State has left dozens dead, homes destroyed and residents fearful of another possible attack. Despite previous security measures in the area, the incident has renewed concerns about how vulnerable communities can be better protected.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: At least eight Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: At least eight Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza.
Four-year-old among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli drone attacks across the Gaza Strip.
- Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: Shin Bet accused of coercing Gaza targets into deadly strikes to spare families - report.
The outlet reportedly interviewed several Gazans whom it describes as "Palestinian faction activists," as well as their families, and they all had similar experiences.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Iran has a hidden network of military agencies managing to smuggle hardware past US blockade.
“This is the complete ecosystem of the Iranian military’s trade business," said Miad Maleki, a former senior official at the US Treasury Department who helped design the American sanctions on Iran.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: UAE hopes to avert new Iran conflict, prepares for worst-case scenario.
At a Bahrain security summit, UAE adviser Anwar Gargash called for diplomacy with Iran while warning that Gulf states remain prepared for more conflict.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: 'We're a tech-savvy army': DG ISPR voices confidence in Pakistan's operational readiness for drone warfare.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 'We're a tech-savvy army': DG ISPR voices confidence in Pakistan's operational readiness for drone warfare.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has affirmed that Pakistan is “much ahead” in operational readiness compared to the Afghan Taliban and India, adding that the country’s military is adopting emerging technologies. The military spokesperson’s remarks, aired on local media on Sunday, were made during Friday’s wide-ranging interview with Reuters. The remarks focused on the ongoing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes.
Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the US and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: US hears Pakistan’s concerns over terrorism from Afghanistan, would play ‘productive role’ if there is one: Rubio.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday said that Washington has “heard” Pakistan’s concerns about terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and if “there’s a productive role for us to play, we would play it”. Rubio’s statement came in response to a question about tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan at a press talks in Atlanta. “Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan. They feel as if the Taliban have not done enough to constrain those attacks, and they have taken action against it.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NK News, The Hindu - International, Yonhap News Agency, one hour ago: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads: KCNA.
North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported on Sunday, the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them. The test, conducted on Saturday, came after the nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile. It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded.
India - bottom line: China's mysterious submarine could give US Navy a Pacific nightmare.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: China's mysterious submarine could give US Navy a Pacific nightmare.
China is currently testing an innovative uncrewed trimaran submarine that boasts an arsenal of missiles, designed to significantly strengthen its military presence against US naval forces in the Indo-Pacific. This submarine could possess between 16 and 18 of China's cutting-edge YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship missiles. Its tactics may feature submerging before launching surprise missile strikes on enemy ships, presenting serious implications for US Navy strategic operations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Another 'exploding pager' plot? Israel eyes strike on Tehran’s top military bosses.
Israel is considering a covert operation similar to its previous attacks targeting Iran's military leadership. Former Mossad official Oded Ailam mentioned key Iranian figures that might be targeted for elimination. The planned operation follows Israel's successful 2024 campaign against Hezbollah which involved explosive communication devices. Military operations against Iran may resume after the upcoming US midterm elections in November.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Delaware couple wins land dispute after neighbours demand $30,000.
After two decades of contention, a Delaware court officially awarded Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray ownership of a long-disputed parcel of land. The case arose when the Preradovic family challenged property lines after purchasing an adjacent lot. Failed negotiations led to litigation, ultimately resulting in the court granting the Murrays the rear yard while their claims to the front areas were rejected.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Violent protests rock Bangladesh garment hubs as workers demand pay hike.
The unrest, which began on Saturday, escalated on Sunday in industrial areas such as Mirpur in Dhaka and Konabari in Gazipur. Protesters allegedly vandalised factories, attacked police outposts with stones and set police vehicles on fire. Several major roads were blocked using barricades, disrupting movement. Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds as demonstrations intensified.

The Azini was hijacked on Thursday between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said on Sunday. The 2026 Global Governance Forum in Xiongan, Hebei province, wrapped up on October 25. Against a backdrop of acute strains on multilateralism and a widening global governance deficit, the forum galvanised a shared sense of urgency across the international community for reform and solidarity. - South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: From rifles to radar: China upgrades its African arms trade as Russia and the West retreat.
For decades, China has supplied African militaries with small arms and land-based equipment such as armoured vehicles, trucks and artillery. Now, it is selling them more specialised weapons, including armed drones and electronic warfare systems. Analysts noted that China’s African arms sales were shifting qualitatively to air-defence systems, armed drones and electronic warfare gear once dominated by Russia and the West. - South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: Armour vs altitude: India’s light tank dilemma along China border.
India’s new high-altitude combat tank was designed to go where its heavier armoured fighting vehicles cannot: the thin mountain air, narrow roads and small bridges along its disputed border with China. In its base configuration, the Zorawar weighs some 25 tonnes – light enough to be flown all the way to the Line of Actual Control – but a push to make it strong enough to withstand high-calibre autocannon fire could add an extra seven tonnes to that loadout. A French officer described "skin that stings" after being set alight by a molotov cocktail during another weekend of protests in Paris.
